newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to restructure the state regie autonomes.
newsitem.headline: Romania to restructure the state regie autonomes.

text.p: Romania will restructure its "regies autonomes" (state-owned firms), which make up the core of its economy, in a major step to speed reforms in line with suggestions made by international lenders, the reform minister said on Wednesday.
"Our plan is to reorganise the regies autonomes by restructuring them, splitting them into smaller firms, or creating companies of national interest," Ulm Spineanu told a news conference.
Romania's privatisation programme, launched in 1995 after long delays, has so far failed to tackle the regies autonomes that include large utilities and strategic industrial sectors.
"This is a major move for reforms and a big change in our economy," Spineanu said.
Most of the regies autonomes generate huge losses as they are affected by financial bottlenecks in the economy.
Real privatisation was delayed by the leftist cabinet ousted in last November's elections by a reformist coalition.
Western lenders had made fresh loans conditional on the restructuring of oversized industries inherited from the former communists.

Francois Ettori, the World Bank's resident representative in Bucharest said on Wednesday the Bank was expected this week to approve the resumption of $80 million in credits to back the industrial restructuring process.
Spineanu said some of the firms created after the split of the regies autonomes would be turned into "national companies", which could eventually be partly privatised.
"The private share in such companies could amount to up to 49 percent," Spineanu said. "The (state) Tarom airline could be a good example of such a national company."
